title: What does each rewind option restore?
intro: You asked for a refactor, Claude edited several files, and you want to go back. You open the rewind menu, select the prompt that started it, and choose an action.

show.title: Files and conversation both go back
show.detail: The tracked file edits are reverted and the conversation returns to the selected prompt, which is placed back in the input so you can edit or resend it.

trace.text: Reverts the files Claude edited to their state at that prompt.
Rewinds the conversation to the same point.

show.title: Conversation goes back, files stay
show.detail: The conversation returns to the selected message while your code stays as it is now.

trace.text: Rewinds the conversation to that message.

show.title: Files go back, conversation stays
show.detail: The file changes are reverted while the conversation is kept. Files changed only by shell commands are not tracked, so use Git for those.

show.title: Nothing is undone; context is freed
show.detail: The conversation from that point on is compressed into a summary. Files on disk do not change, and the original messages remain in the session transcript.

trace.text: Replaces the later messages with a summary.
Leaves every file as it is.

fallback.title: Pick an action
fallback.detail: This demo scripts four actions of the rewind menu. Choose one to see what it restores.

quiz.question: Claude ran a shell command that changed a file it never edited with its editing tools. Will /rewind restore that file?
options: No, use version control such as Git
quiz.explanation: A file that only shell commands changed is not tracked by checkpoints and stays as it is.
